records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dark-theme branch for this link uses lightness 70% where every sibling change in the PR inverts the light theme value (30% dark-becomes-light 70%), producing a dark-mode value that no longer matches the intended visual weight. Users of dark themes get links styled at a different visual weight than light-theme users at the same site; also suggests a copy-paste error that the next maintainer will silently propagate. Rebuttal (author may have intentionally matched adjacent 50% values) fails because the light-mode value was left at 30%, breaking the inversion pattern the PR title claims.
records.rationale: The finding claims the *dark-theme branch* uses lightness 70% while the light-theme value was left at 30%. But in the only suspicious change of this form (desktop/topic-post.scss), the code is `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`—i.e., 70% is on the first (light-theme) argument and 30% is on the second (dark-theme) argument, directly contradicting the finding’s description.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] mobile/modal.scss .custom-message-length dark branch is inverted relative to the desktop/modal.scss counterpart (primary 30%/secondary 70% here vs primary 70%/secondary 30% on desktop). Mobile dark-theme users see the message-length hint at full-strength color while desktop dark users see it muted; the two parallel hand-maintained rules have drifted in the same PR, so a future fix will have to remember both sites. Rebuttal (intentional mobile-specific contrast) fails because no other mobile/desktop pair in this diff diverges in polarity.
records.rationale: The diff shows an inconsistency between desktop and mobile modal hint colors for the same selector. In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` is changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`, while in `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` it is changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. This verifies the "inverted polarity" claim and the drift between parallel hand-maintained rules, but the diff alone cannot prove the UX
